outline: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia / disorders of steroid biosynthesis
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: POR transfers electrons from NADPH to microsomal cytochrome P450 enzymes in the endoplasmic reticulum, including CYP17A1, CYP21A2, and CYP19A1. Loss of POR therefore produces a combined steroidogenic defect rather than deficiency of a single adrenal enzyme.
vignette: A newborn with a 46,XY karyotype has micropenis and severe hypospadias. Examination also shows craniosynostosis and radiohumeral synostosis. The mother developed acne, deepening of the voice, and increased facial hair during pregnancy despite no androgen use. Steroid profiling in the infant suggests combined impairment of 17α-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase and 21-hydroxylase activities. Sequencing identifies pathogenic variants in POR.
lead: Which of the following molecular defects best explains this infant's abnormal steroidogenesis?
correct: Reduced transfer of electrons from NADPH to multiple microsomal cytochrome P450 enzymes in the endoplasmic reticulum
distractors: Defective transport of cholesterol from the outer to the inner mitochondrial membrane
Reduced transfer of electrons from ferredoxin to mitochondrial CYP11A1 and CYP11B enzymes
Failure to convert Δ5 steroids to their corresponding Δ4 steroids in the adrenal cortex and gonads
Selective loss of 21-hydroxylase activity with preserved CYP17A1 and aromatase function
distractor_notes: StAR deficiency impairs mitochondrial cholesterol delivery and broadly reduces steroidogenesis, but it does not explain the characteristic combined microsomal P450 defect caused by POR loss.
Ferredoxin-dependent electron transfer supports mitochondrial steroidogenic P450 enzymes. POR instead supplies electrons to microsomal P450 enzymes in the endoplasmic reticulum.

HSD3B2 deficiency blocks conversion of pregnenolone, 17-hydroxypregnenolone, and DHEA to their Δ4 products; it is a single-enzyme defect, not a shared electron-donor defect affecting several microsomal P450 enzymes.
CYP21A2 deficiency can cause congenital adrenal hyperplasia but cannot explain simultaneous impairment of CYP17A1 and aromatase-related pathways.
key_expl: PORD is caused by pathogenic variants in POR, which encodes the flavoprotein electron donor for microsomal cytochrome P450 enzymes. POR accepts electrons from NADPH and transfers them to enzymes including CYP17A1, CYP21A2, and CYP19A1. Consequently, POR deficiency can mimic a combination of 17α-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase and 21-hydroxylase deficiencies and can also impair aromatase activity, helping explain genital atypia and maternal virilization.
objective: Explain P450 oxidoreductase deficiency as failure of NADPH-dependent electron transfer to multiple microsomal steroidogenic cytochrome P450 enzymes.
clues: combined CYP17A1 and CYP21A2 biochemical pattern
